Day 8 – Pick2Pack with RightHand Robotics, Inc 

Today we Pick2Pack with RightHand Robotics, Inc and their AI-powered RightPick robotic piece-picking system, designed to autonomously pick individual items and seamlessly connect with automated packaging workflows.

RightPick identifies and picks individual SKUs with no prior training and places them directly into CMC’s patented Vary-Tote or onto the induction belts of CMC Packaging Automation packaging systems such as CMC CartonWrap and CMC Genesys.

Experience Pick2Pack workflow at LogiMAT Trade Show (Booth ES55) and #MODEX 2026 (Booth B8904) and see how autonomous piece picking and right-sized packaging work together to drive reliable, high-performance fulfillment.

Thanks to RightHand Robotics, Inc for this collaboration.

50% more installations year over year. More than tripled our bookings. And our partners are deploying systems on their own, no RightHanders required.

Thank you to Chris Lingamfelter and RoboAdvisors for capturing the day on video, and to Greg Bellon, Sanjay Aggarwal (F-Prime Capital), and Dave Johnson (TRI) for bringing such a thoughtful perspective to the panel discussion.

We had such a great time, that we're planning on making this an annual event. If you want to experience it for yourself sooner, our HQ is just 15 minutes from Logan Airport in Boston, and we always love having visitors.

repost.content:
Robotic piece picking is quietly getting very real.
I spent the day at RightHand Robotics’ Boston-area headquarters, and I came away impressed.
It had been about a year since my last visit — and the progress is obvious.
✔ ~50% installation growth in the past year
✔ Partner-led deployments without RightHand engineers onsite
✔ More mature workflows and real production experience
✔ Clear momentum toward lights-out fulfillment
RightHand has been working on robotic piece picking for over a decade — and it shows. This isn’t lab technology anymore. These are real systems solving real fulfillment problems.
Always valuable to see the technology up close and talk with customers and partners who are actually running it.
Thanks to Yaro Tenzer and the RightHand Robotics, Inc. team for hosting a great open house. Tip of the hat to team lead Jake Tobin and to the rest of the Robot Advisors team for their support. 
If piece picking automation is on your roadmap, this is a company worth paying attention to.
